title: Converting Error Types
goal: Understand how the try operator uses the From trait to convert error types automatically.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Morning: Error Handling

sections.text: Functions often execute multiple operations that return different error types. Reading a file produces `io::Error`, while parsing numbers produces `ParseIntError`.

sections.caption: Fails to compile because types do not match.

sections.text: The `?` operator expands to `return Err(From::from(err))` on error. It automatically converts error types if an implementation of `From` exists.

sections.caption: Implementing From enables automatic conversion with the try operator.

sections.text: If no `From` implementation exists, you can convert errors manually using `.map_err()`.

explanation: Understand how the try operator uses the From trait to convert error types automatically.
